_comment: Extra update sources for the Shelly Updater DankBar plugin.
Copied to ~/.config/DankMaterialShell/shelly-updater-sources.json on first run;
edit that copy, not this file. Changes are picked up on the next plugin reload:
dms ipc call plugins reload shellyUpdater
SECURITY: listCmd / applyAll / applyOne are executed as you. Treat a sources
file from someone else exactly like a shell script from someone else.
Fields:
id                short unique name; also the settings key and chip label
label             shown in the menu
icon              Material Symbol name (fonts.google.com/icons)
bin               command that must exist, else the source is hidden entirely
listCmd           argv that prints what is outdated
parse             how to read that output — see the two forms below
applyAll          argv updating everything (omit to make the source read-only)
applyOne          argv updating one item; {id} {name} {current} {latest}
minIntervalHours  how long results stay cached (network sources: keep this high)
readOnly          true = never applied in-widget, only handed to a terminal
note              one-line caveat shown under the menu row
enabled           false to keep an entry without using it
env               NAME: value pairs prepended to the command; values may use $HOME/$PATH.
Needed for version-manager tools (nvm, pyenv, asdf) — see npmGlobal.
parse: { type: 'regex', pattern, flags?, name, id?, current?, latest?,
strip?, versionText?, exclude?[] }   — capture-group NUMBERS
parse: { type: 'json', root?, iterate, name, id?, current?, latest?,
description?, require? }             — dotted paths; '$key' = object key

sources.label: npm (global)
sources._note: env pins the toolchain. The widget's commands run in the DMS service environment, NOT your shell — so an nvm/pyenv/asdf-managed tool otherwise resolves to a different install than the one you use, and you get updates reported for packages you never touch. Point PATH at your own node bin dir (and update it when you change node versions). Delete this env block if your npm is system-wide. Keep values simple: they are emitted inside double quotes, so $HOME and $PATH expand but nested quoting will not work.

sources.label: Flatpak (unmanaged remotes)
sources.note: Listing only — apply through Shelly's Flatpak source
